Students registered in this online OL1 lecture must also register for the online OQ1 discussion section. For students who have some prior knowledge of chemistry. Principles governing atomic structure, bonding, states of matter, stoichiometry, and chemical equilibrium. Credit is not given for both CHEM 102 and CHEM 202. CHEM 102 and CHEM 103 are approved for General Education credit only as a sequence. Both courses must be completed to receive Natural Science and Technology credit. Prerequisite: Credit in or exemption from MATH 112; one year of high school chemistry or equivalent. All students enrolled in CHEM 102 should also enroll in CHEM 103. Students must register for a combination of one lecture and one quiz (also called Discussion) section beginning with the same letter. "Online CHEM 102O is NOT a completely asynchronous online class. This online class has a one-hour live, mandatory class called a Lesson Review, that is held twice weekly in a Zoom classroom with students, the professor and teaching assistants all working together. The content of each chemistry topic being taught is shared with students using pre-recorded lesson videos in the form of playlists and the professor also provides detailed class notes for each topic. The reason why these mandatory Lesson Reviews are held twice a week is to attempt to help all students effectively review one chemistry topic during each class, with the primary focus of each class being the teaching of problem-solving techniques that involve students being shown how to apply and then being asked to apply the content of each chemistry topic. These problem-solving techniques are critical, as students have a weekly online quiz, homework, and other assignments on the 2 chemistry topics that are covered each week. Effective problem-solving techniques are modeled throughout each Lesson Review, former Exam problems are done, and very helpful exam information and exam-taking techniques are shared. Graded clicker questions are also asked during these mandatory, live, Lesson Reviews to help students and the professor evaluate the understanding of each chemistry topic that is reviewed during each one-hour class. Students taking this class in the Fall and Spring will also be expected to come to the UIUC campus to take all Exams, which will be proctored by the instructor and your teaching assistants. Students are strongly encouraged to reach out to the professor of this online CHEM 102 class via email with any additional questions about how the online class is structured, before registering for this online class and before the start date of the class.”

This 2-credit hour course will explore the properties of coffee and its attributes from the perspective of chemistry, biology, ecology, and nutrition as well as the social and community impact of coffee production.

This 3-credit hour course will explore the properties of coffee as described for (CHEM-199 2ch) but will add a study abroad component that will allow students to witness all stages of coffee production, as well as community involvement at a coffee farm in Panama.

sections.sectionText: Students must register for both the "DA2" in-person Lecture and an "DD" in-person discussion." A continuation of CHEM 232, this course focuses on advanced reaction mechanisms and the chemistry of complex organic molecules. Students will engage with practical applications in organic synthesis throughout the course. Topics include the reactions of conjugated compounds under kinetic and thermodynamic conditions, the exploration of pericyclic reactions, and the role of heteroatoms in aromaticity, as well as electrophilic aromatic substitution. The course also covers reactions involving carbonyl compounds, amines, and carboxylic acid derivatives. Additionally, students will be introduced to biochemically relevant molecules such as carbohydrates, lipids, proteins, and nucleic acids. Materials Required Textbook: Organic Chemistry by Janice Gorzynski Smith 7th Edition. Online Homework: ALEXS. Day1Access course materials cost $129.41. For more information see https://go.illinois.edu/Day1Access.
